session.question: What link between the consumer and the Circular economy is denoted in the context, and what is said about it?
session.answer:
The context denotes a consumer–circular economy link as a relationship through sustainable consumption, where consumers are not passive end users but actors whose purchasing choices can support or hinder circular systems. In the cited review, this link is described as an important issue in the literature on sustainable consumption, but also as difficult and not straightforward because of the complexity of “being” a sustainable consumer and the theoretical fragmentation of the field. (vargasmerino2023sustainableconsumptionconceptualization chunk 1)

More specifically, the context highlights that consumers connect to the circular economy through purchase intention toward sustainable waste-to-value (WTV, waste-to-value) foods. In this case, consumer willingness to buy determines whether circular products are adopted, and the study treats consumer habits, perceptions, origin information, nutritional information, education, and socio-demographic traits as key determinants of that willingness. The paper also frames WTV foods as a concrete expression of circular economy processes because they convert excess material into higher-value food products. (ali2021analysisofcircular chunk 1)

Overall, the denoted link is behavioral and decision-based: consumer demand is a mechanism through which circular economy practices gain or lose viability, but the relationship is complex and mediated by multiple informational and socio-demographic factors. (vargasmerino2023sustainableconsumptionconceptualization chunk 1, ali2021analysisofcircular chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-e694c0f1: The excerpt links consumers to the circular economy through their purchasing intentions: consumers can either support or hinder the circular economy by deciding whether to buy sustainable Waste-to-Value (WTV) foods. The paper says consumer reaction is very strong for these products, so evaluating consumer habits and perceptions is essential for understanding circular systems. It also notes that WTV foods demonstrate circular economy processes by converting excess material into new food with higher nutritional properties. The study investigates which factors shape consumers’ willingness to buy such foods, including product origin, production/nutritional information, education, and socio-demographic traits.
From Shahjahan Ali, Shahnaj Akter, and Csaba Fogarassy. Analysis of circular thinking in consumer purchase intention to buy sustainable waste-to-value (wtv) foods. Sustainability, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su13105390, doi:10.3390/su13105390.

pqac-82240a3c: The excerpt states that the review denoted a link between the consumer and the circular economy, emphasizing the difficulties behind that interaction. It presents this relationship as one of the key issues discussed in the literature on sustainable consumption. The paper suggests that, alongside the complexity of being a green/sustainable consumer, the consumer–circular economy connection is important but not straightforward, reflecting broader conceptual complexity and theoretical fragmentation in the field.
From Jorge Alberto Vargas-Merino, Cristian Armando Ríos-Lama, and Miguel Humberto Panez-Bendezú. Sustainable consumption: conceptualization and characterization of the complexity of “being” a sustainable consumer—a systematic review of the scientific literature. Sustainability, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su15108401, doi:10.3390/su15108401.

pqac-96f5ab96: The excerpt explains that the study applies the circular economy principle of “reusing” to pre-consumer waste from apparel production. It describes a shortest-loop process of gathering, sorting, redesigning, re-cutting, and sewing waste into new circular products, such as toddler t-shirts. The text suggests this direct reutilization is more environmentally sustainable and economically feasible than recycling, landfilling, or incineration. However, it focuses on factory pre-consumer waste and production processes rather than an explicit consumer-circular economy relationship.
From Upama Nasrin Haq and S.M. Rakifull Alam. Implementing circular economy principles in the apparel production process: reusing pre-consumer waste for sustainability of environment and economy. Cleaner Waste Systems, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clwas.2023.100108, doi:10.1016/j.clwas.2023.100108.

pqac-3e8df035: The excerpt explains that circular economy practices are tied to how countries produce, consume, and waste, especially in the energy sector. It emphasizes that consumers are part of this broader circular economy context because shifting consumption patterns is necessary to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and meet climate goals. The article focuses mainly on renewable energy as a circular economy tool for sustainable development, rather than detailing a specific consumer-behavior model. It states that efficient implementation of circular economy and renewable energy practices is needed to achieve SDGs, and that EU countries should better use renewable energy potential to support clean energy transition.
From Ugnius Jakubelskas and Viktorija Skvarciany. Circular economy practices as a tool for sustainable development in the context of renewable energy: what are the opportunities for the eu? Oeconomia Copernicana, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.24136/oc.2023.025, doi:10.24136/oc.2023.025.

pqac-f3089aac: The excerpt discusses the circular economy mainly in terms of mineral resource management and economic security in Ukraine. It says the circular economy integrates several economic security components (environmental, industrial, energy, mineral resource, social, food) and is linked to ecological-economic system formation. However, it does not specifically mention any relationship or link between the consumer and the circular economy, nor does it describe consumer-related effects or roles in detail.
From Kateryna Markevych, S. Maistro, Viktor Koval, and Viktor Paliukh. Mining sustainability and circular economy in the context of economic security in ukraine. Mining of Mineral Deposits, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.33271/mining16.01.101, doi:10.33271/mining16.01.101.
